key_and_prompt_notes.finding: Retained non-novel regression questions as disclosed; neither is a fresh coverage discovery. Current Q100 stipulates cleanup after the full tree and correctly avoids conflating it with the failed-Drown Push asked by Q113.

Current fixed key correctly limits general bonuses to eligible printed Range arrows, excludes boosting another Range boost and another Spirit action, and keeps source/target restrictions. No excluded Sky example appears in the current question or key.
Speed change, simultaneous Blight and repeated Ravages are express scenario givens. They do not name/import excluded producers. Apply the sourced generic rule to those givens.

Ordinary available-piece and legal-target assumptions apply. Q67 contains separate solo and transferred-card clauses; the transfer clause is not asserted to involve a second Spirit in that solo game. Q71 only permits choosing actual available disks.

The current raw Mists face says Damage to each Invader; Q97 says it damages each Town/City without asserting only buildings are damaged. This narrower stated fact remains true, and its building-survival/source-boost answers are correct.

Independently recomputed Ravage arithmetic, checked efficient Dahan Damage, simultaneous land/Dahan timing, additive and reusable Defend, Dahan-only protection, ignored partial land Damage and persistent piece Damage. The fixed answers are consistent.

Independently checked Repeat and trigger temporal units: modifiers persist, no Repeat chaining, distinct Powerstorm choices, lost Elements rechecked, forgotten cards unavailable for ordinary later Repeat, finite Vengeance recursion, newest speed, internal bonus nonstacking, no extra card play, failed-Drown Push before cleanup and default retargeting.

coverage_gaps.rule: Ordinary Growth selects one complete option; separate sections are alternative choices unless explicitly overridden.
coverage_gaps.question: A Spirit has several separate Growth options and no instruction allowing more than one choice. During one Spirit Phase, may it combine the Energy action from one option with the Add Presence action from a different option, or must it choose a single entire option?
coverage_gaps.predetermined_answer: It must choose one entire Growth option and perform all possible actions in that option. It may not combine actions from separate options or select multiple options without an explicit instruction permitting that. The actions within the chosen option may be performed in any order.

source.anchor: CORE p.8 Spirit Phase, Grow step: Choose one option; Each section is a single choice

coverage_gaps.novelty_reason: The changed outcome is whether actions from two alternative Growth options are legal. This is the printed one-option choice rule, not changed numbers or a mechanical recombination. Q02 assumes an option with two Add Presence actions and asks chaining/track selection. Q24 asks impossible instructions, explicit costs, mandatory actions and waiting on another Spirit. Q74 asks ordering of the multiple choices explicitly allowed to Rampant Green. None asks how many ordinary options may be selected, or whether instructions from different options can be combined. A respondent can answer all those prompts correctly while incorrectly allowing multiple ordinary options. The map row Spirit phase Growth maps the paragraph to those questions, but that mapping does not request this first sentence.

coverage_gaps.rule: A printed Power Range is a maximum, permitting closer targets as well as targets at the printed distance.
coverage_gaps.question: An ordinary land-targeting Power has printed Range 1, Target ANY and no special origin requirement. Your Presence is in land A, and land B is adjacent to A. Assuming all other restrictions are met, may you target A as well as B, or must the target be exactly one land away from your Presence?
coverage_gaps.predetermined_answer: Both A and B are legal targets. Printed Range 1 is a maximum, so Range 0 is allowed: A contains your Presence and B is one land away. The Power does not have to target a land exactly one away.

source.anchor: CORE p.16 Anatomy of Powers, Range: This is a maximum; you can always use a shorter Range

coverage_gaps.novelty_reason: This tests the explicit permission to use a Power closer than its printed Range. Q21 asks whether a land is within Range 1 of itself, a distance relation, and Q28 asks what a printed Range 0 target requires and which nonnumeric requirements a boost cannot waive. Neither asks whether the Range number printed on a Power is a maximum or an exact target distance. Q114 asks retargeting between legal lands without asking what makes a closer land legal. This is not a numerical variant: distances deliberately match Q21; the newly requested clause is legality of a closer target under a printed Power Range. A mistaken exact-printed-Range targeting rule can coexist with correct answers to Q21, Q28 and Q114. Do not infer this permission from the map label Power anatomy Range/Target or unstated background legal-target knowledge.

material_coverage_false_positives.missing_clause: Choose one ordinary option; each section is a single alternative choice.
Printed Power Range is a maximum and permits closer targeting.

nonblocking_map_precision_notes: The infinite-vitality FAQ row still lists Q100 although current Q100 asks only post-tree cleanup. Its protection and failed-Drown branches are requested by Q65/Q113/Q117/Q118, so this stale individual mapping is not a new gap.
